items.text: Held Friday through Sunday in Atlanta, Georgia, the Dogwood Festival is the city’s oldest fine arts festival. Dogwood trees are in full bloom, and artists from around the country display their work. All art is welcome, from paintings to photographs and sculptures to jewelry. There’s also music and food to round out the celebrations. Created in 1936 to boost community spirit during the Great Depression and celebrate Atlanta’s native dogwood trees. items.text: Neurodiversity Pride Day was created in 2018 by the Neurodiversity Foundation to recognize and embrace neurological differences. It’s a day organized by neurodivergent people, for neurodivergent people, and their allies. This is part of a broader Neurodiversity Pride Week, with events leading up to this day. “Neurodiversity” refers to the idea that differences in how people’s brains work are natural and valuable, not deficits. items.text: National Chicken Noodle Soup Day honors one of the most comforting and iconic soups in American cuisine. Chicken noodle soup brings comfort when it’s cold outside. It’s a traditional remedy when feeling sick. items.text: National Cheese Doodle Day is all about cheese doodles, those bright-orange corn snacks. These puffy, crispy corn snacks coated in cheese go by many names, including cheese puffs, cheese curls, cheese balls, corn curls, and cheese doodles. They were invented in the United States in the 1930s. There are competing accounts on who invented them, but the most accepted credits Morrie Yohai for Old London Foods. items.text: National Ranch Dressing Day is a dedicated to America’s most popular salad dressing, a position held since 1992. The day celebrates ranch dressing, the creamy, tangy condiment used as a salad dressing and as a dip. It’s made with buttermilk, garlic, onion, mustard, herbs (commonly chives, parsley, and dill), and spices.
